messages:
From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.ai>
To: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.ai>, Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.ai>
Date: Sun, 15 Nov 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: FY27 Q1 OKR packet — consolidation, scorecards, and exec signoff

Team —

Thanks for the drafts. I pulled together a consolidated OKR packet (attached) and a first-pass QBR exec deck for the leadership review. Goal here is to close the OKR wording and the top-line scorecards by Wednesday so we can circulate to the board next week.

Asks: 
- Please review the OKR wording and metric definitions in tab "Consolidated_OKRs". Redline any ambiguous success criteria directly in the sheet.
- Marcus: double-check the performance and cost efficiency targets for Serving runtime (we had some open questions after infra's sim runs).
- Laura: confirm CS health metrics and customer targets in the scorecard (page 3 of the deck).
- Vivek: I need a short note (1–2 bullets) on any material risks or dependencies for production parity across regions.
- Lauren: ping me if you want the exec deck to include the escalation runbook in the appendix — I can add.

Timeline: 
- End of day Tue (11/16): in-sheet redlines and comments
- Wed morning (11/17): final sign-off from leadership
- Wed EOD: packet published to Drive and shared with Board liaison

Attachments: FY27Q1_OKRs_consolidated.xlsx, QBR_FY27Q1_exec_deck_v3.pptx

I'm keeping the deck intentionally compact (8 slides) — we just need top-line ask, key metrics, highlights, and 2–3 risks with mitigations.

Thanks,
Hannah
Hannah Schmitt
Head of Product Operations | Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: FY27 Q1 OKR packet — consolidation, scorecards, and exec signoff

Hannah —

Saw this first thing. Quick notes after scanning the Serving runtime targets:
- Cost per 1k tokens target on slide 4: I adjusted the number in the sheet (tab "Serving") — we can hit the lower bound if we layer the 8-bit quantization plan plus aggressive batching, but that assumes the two kernel patches land on time. I marked a dependency row.
- Throughput SLOs: suggesting we specify median p95 and 99th separately (users care about 99th tail). I added a comment in the deck where p99 is missing.
- Also added a short note listing infra's planned canary dates — helps QBR timeline context.

No major blockers from infra — just the kernel patch schedule and GPU availability for Dedicated tests.

-Marcus
Marcus Lin
VP, Infrastructure | Redwood Inference

- Regional parity risk: APAC region may lag by 3–4 weeks due to an external scheduler dependency; mitigation: temporary routing to hosted region + accelerated Dedicated testing in week 2.

-Vivek
